statements.text: Started this week as a pastry chef at Maison Verdier here in Lyon. The croissants alone are worth the 4am alarm.
Renting a tiny studio in Croix-Rousse, fifth floor, no elevator. My calves are filing a complaint.
My tabby Biscotte is six and deeply offended whenever I'm home on a Sunday.
I cycle to work along the Rhône, about 25 minutes if the wind behaves.
Trying to learn Spanish with Duolingo, ten minutes in bed every night before I pass out.
I'm allergic to hazelnuts, which is a cruel joke for a pastry chef. Always carry my epi pen.
Mornings start with a double espresso from my stovetop moka pot, no sugar, no conversation.
My boyfriend Théo is a sound engineer at a little radio station near Part-Dieu.
My phone is a Samsung Galaxy S21 and the battery dies by lunchtime.
Running 5k loops in Parc de la Tête d'Or every Tuesday and Thursday evening.
Khruangbin's Mordechai is my go-to album for baking days.
Doctor told me to cut the caffeine, so it's genmaicha tea in the mornings now.
Adopted a second cat from the shelter, a shy little black one called Madeleine.
Handed in my notice at Maison Verdier. Starting at Café Lumière next Monday as head of pastry!
Unboxed an iPhone 16 today and the camera is unreal for food shots.
Théo and I finally moved into a two-bedroom in Villeurbanne, with an actual elevator.
Vet says Biscotte weighs a chunky seven kilos, so she's on a diet and furious about it.
Café Lumière is across town, so it's tram T1 for me now and I finally get to read on my commute.
Knee has been angry since May and the doctor banned running. Swimming twice a week at the municipal pool instead.
Also signed up for Italian classes on Tuesday evenings, because why suffer in just one language.
Had dinner with my sister Inès at that Lebanese place on Friday and she cried over the baklava.
Lux by Rosalía is what I bake to lately.
Turns out I'm also mildly allergic to kiwi, my mouth went itchy at brunch.
Plot twist: I'm back on coffee, but strictly decaf, from the old moka pot.
Théo quit the radio and is now a sound designer at a video game studio in Lyon.

statements.text: School year kicks off on Monday. I've taught physics and maths at Älvsborgsskolan for 27 years and somehow still enjoy it.
We live in a red villa in Mölndal, just outside Gothenburg, with white corners naturally.
I drive a 2014 Volvo V70 diesel with 240,000 km on the clock and zero plans to part with it.
Our dog Sture is a nine-year-old golden retriever who treats every walk like a polar expedition.
Sture gets three kilometres every morning at 6, rain or shine. Bought myself a headlamp for the dark months.
Blood pressure was a bit high at my checkup, so it's 5 mg of amlodipine every morning for me.
My laptop is a ThinkPad T480 that I refuse to retire.
Wednesday evenings I'm at a woodworking course, building a Shaker-style cabinet.
My daughter Linnea works as a veterinarian up in Uppsala, mostly horses and the occasional angry goat.
Karin drives a white Toyota Yaris hybrid and brags about the fuel economy constantly.
Traded in the old Volvo for a second-hand Nissan Leaf. It's so quiet the dog doesn't hear me coming.
Blood pressure still stubborn, so the doctor doubled my amlodipine to 10 mg.
The woodworking course wrapped up last night. Cabinet is finished and now lives in our hallway.
Karin and I took in a one-eyed cat called Pelle who adopted us, more or less.
Sture's hips are getting bad, so mornings are a gentle one kilometre these days.
Typing this on my new MacBook Air and the battery just keeps going and going.
Left the classroom for good. I'm a lab instructor at Chalmers' physics department now, no more teenagers hiding phones under desks.
Sailing season is open, so I race a Laser dinghy with the Mölndal club on Sunday mornings.
Karin's boss at the pharmacy, Mattias, bakes cardamom buns for the whole team every Friday.
Ankles swelled up like balloons, so the doctor swapped the amlodipine for losartan.
The Leaf's winter range was a joke, so I swapped it for a used Skoda Enyaq.
The Enyaq is the 80 version in dark green and the dog crate fits in the back perfectly.
Went to a tribute concert for Esbjörn Svensson at the Konserthuset on Friday, goosebumps all night.
Unpacking boxes in our new place in Linné, central Gothenburg is a lot louder than Mölndal ever was.
Also joined a men's choir, we rehearse Tuesday nights and I'm a second tenor.

statements.text: I design interfaces for a fintech startup called Finlo here in Bangalore, so my days are Figma and arguing about button radii.
My manager Divya is great, she actually reads my design docs.
Sharing a three-bedroom flat in Indiranagar with two roommates and the rent is eye-watering.
I scooter to the office every day, 35 minutes if Old Airport Road behaves.
Phone is a OnePlus 9, still going strong after three years.
I've been vegetarian my whole life, mom would disown me otherwise.
Saturday mornings are badminton with the Koramangala crew, 7am sharp.
Learning Kannada because my landlord only speaks Kannada and I'm tired of smiling and nodding.
Planning to apply for the HCI master's at TU Delft, deadline's in December.
My brother Arjun works at Infosys in Pune, backend stuff he refuses to explain.
My scooter is a matte grey Honda Activa that I bought second-hand from a colleague.
Project Lotus ships on 15 December so everyone on the team is sleeping under their desks.
Project Atlas, the other thing I'm on, isn't due until the end of January.
Reorg at work. Karthik is my manager now and Divya moved over to the payments team.
All my work notes live in Notion, with a color-coded system nobody else understands.
My roommate Sneha is a corporate lawyer, she bills more per hour than I earn per day.
The camera on my iPhone 15 makes my food photos look way better than they deserve.
Iron was low at my checkup, so I'm no longer strictly vegetarian, eggs are in.
Decided to skip the Delft master's. The money goes toward a flat down payment instead.
Last Friday was my last day at Finlo, and tomorrow I start as a senior product designer at Orchard Health.
My manager at Orchard is Meera, ex-Google, asks scary good questions.
Orchard's office is right by the Purple Line so I take the metro now, the scooter's just collecting dust in the parking lot.
Moved into my own 1BHK in HSR Layout, first time living alone and it's glorious.
Also picked up French on Duolingo, purely for fun.
Switched from badminton to bouldering, Saturday mornings at a climbing gym in HSR.
Saw Prateek Kuhad live at Palace Grounds on Friday and my voice is completely gone.
Started using Obsidian for my personal notes, Notion stays for work stuff.

statements.text: Work-wise I'm a freelance photographer, mostly weddings and corporate headshots around São Paulo.
We rent an apartment in Vila Madalena, third floor, and the neighbours' samba nights are free entertainment.
My camera body is a Canon R6, about 40k frames through it so far.
Driving a Fiat Argo, perfect for squeezing into São Paulo parking spots.
Lucas is eight and goes to Colégio Santa Maria, he's obsessed with dinosaurs.
Our dog Pipoca is a three-year-old caramel vira-lata who steals socks.
My phone's a Moto G54, cheap and cheerful.
Jiu-jitsu Tuesday and Thursday nights, still a blue belt after two years.
Trying low-carb since last month, no rice, no bread, brutal in Brazil.
My wife Camila is a dentist with her own clinic in Pinheiros.
Bia just turned five and goes to a little school called Pequeno Príncipe, comes home covered in paint every day.
My brother Thiago drives a black Jeep Renegade and thinks it makes him an adventurer.
Sold the Canon and picked up a Sony A7 IV, the autofocus tracking is witchcraft.
Camila's phone is a Pixel 8 and she never lets me forget its camera beats mine.
Low-carb lasted four months, I'm back on rice and beans like a normal Brazilian.
Joined Estúdio Lume as lead photographer, so no more chasing invoices as a freelancer.
Filmed Lucas's school recital on my new iPhone 15 Pro and the stabilization is absurd.
Traded the Argo for a Hyundai HB20 with automatic transmission, my left leg thanks me.
We moved to a house in Granja Viana, forty minutes outside the city, and finally have a garden.
New house, new school: Lucas goes to Escola Vila Verde now and made a best friend named Davi in week one.
The new place has a little yard where Lucas is building a football goal out of PVC pipes.
Shoulder said enough, so I quit jiu-jitsu. Wednesday night futsal with the neighbourhood guys is my new thing.
We adopted a tiny grey cat from a rescue fair, Bia named her Mel.
Plot twist: the Sony is gone and I'm shooting everything on a Fujifilm X-T5, the film simulations are addictive.
Also picked up a DJI Mini 4 drone for aerial shots, wedding clients go nuts for them.
Shot a wedding in Campos do Jordão last Saturday, eleven hours on my feet.

statements.text: Walt and I have lived in the same two-story house in Westerville, Ohio, for 31 years.
I drive a 2015 Buick Encore, it's been a faithful little car.
I still use a flip phone. I don't see why anyone needs more than that.
My knee replacement is scheduled for December 8th, wish me luck.
My cat Marmalade is seventeen and sleeps on my side of the bed.
Every night I take an atorvastatin for my cholesterol, right before bed.
Surgery went fine! I'm getting around the house on a walker for now.
Walt still works Saturdays at the hardware store, says retirement is overrated.
I wear Phonak hearing aids and the left one keeps whistling at me.
Book club meets the first Thursday of every month at the library.
Monday mornings you'll find me in the hospital gift shop, thirty-eight years of nursing and I still can't stay away.
The walker is gone, just a cane now, and the physical therapist says I'm ahead of schedule.
My daughter Jenny and her family live in Seattle, I'm visiting them in June.
We adopted a rescue beagle named Hank, three years old and howls at the mailman.
Jenny set me up with an iPhone SE and now I'm texting the grandkids emojis nonstop.
I also joined a knitting circle at church, Fridays at ten.
Traded the Buick for a Subaru Forester, higher seats are kinder to the new knee.
The Forester is forest green, which Walt thinks is hilarious.
Walt still drives that 2008 F-150 he refuses to sell.
Muscle aches had my doctor swap the atorvastatin for rosuvastatin.
Cane's in the closet, I walked the whole neighborhood loop without it today!
Got new rechargeable Oticon hearing aids, no more fumbling with tiny batteries.
We sold the old house and moved into a one-floor ranch in Hilliard, no stairs at all.
Marmalade passed away last night, curled up on my side of the bed. I'm a mess.
Book club moved to the second Tuesday evening of the month at Jan's house since the library room got double-booked.
I quit the hospital gift shop, now I read to kids at the library on Monday mornings.
Took my grandson Owen to the zoo on Saturday and he named every single penguin.
